builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
summary: ReLay replaces handcrafting analog layout generator libraries and direct LLM geometry generation by recovering generator programs from existing layouts, then promoting recurring constructions into an evolving reusable function library that LLM agents call instead of emitting raw geometry. Its cost is an up-front reverse-engineering and curation pipeline over layout corpora, dependence on specific PDKs and EDA tooling, and benchmark coverage limited to 1,050 layouts across 27 circuit families and three open-source PDKs. It can fail when held-out layouts contain constructions not yet promoted to the library (learned functions cover only 53-66% of calls), when layouts embed tacit designer intent that geometry recovery misinterprets, and when proprietary PDKs or DRC rules differ from the open-source settings evaluated.
rationale: The cost-reduction result is credible but applies to analog IC layout generation with EDA toolchains and PDK data, so it is relevant only as a transferable pattern unless the reader works in chip design automation.
technique: Layout-to-code recovery with evolving generator library for LLM agents

claims.statement: ReLay replaces handcrafting analog layout generator libraries and direct LLM geometry generation by recovering generator programs from existing layouts, then promoting recurring constructions into an evolving reusable function library that LLM agents call instead of emitting raw geometry. Its cost is an up-front reverse-engineering and curation pipeline over layout corpora, dependence on specific PDKs and EDA tooling, and benchmark coverage limited to 1,050 layouts across 27 circuit families and three open-source PDKs. It can fail when held-out layouts contain constructions not yet promoted to the library (learned functions cover only 53-66% of calls), when layouts embed tacit designer intent that geometry recovery misinterprets, and when proprietary PDKs or DRC rules differ from the open-source settings evaluated.
Frontier LLM agents using ReLay complete new analog layout tasks at 64-77% lower API cost per completed task than direct geometry generation, with comparable completion rates and electrical quality.
